annotation_description: Playing a second Momo when one is already on the battlefield is questionable. Momo is legendary, so casting a second copy will cause both to be put into the graveyard due to the legend rule (or the player keeps the new one and sacrifices the old one, but either way they don't get two Momos). The player loses the existing Momo that was already on board. However, the new Momo does trigger the old Momo's ability (+1/+1 until end of turn for another flying creature entering) before the legend rule applies, but then both die. This wastes a card for essentially no lasting board presence.

Casting Slickshot Show-Off before combat rather than after land drop. The player has a Mountain in hand they could play first to have more mana available during/after combat. More importantly, casting Slickshot pre-combat with Might of the Meek in hand is actually correct for maximizing damage (cast Might during combat to trigger Slickshot's +2/+0), but playing a land first would leave more mana open. With the Mountain played first, they'd have 3 Mountains untapped instead of 2, giving them mana for both Might of the Meek (1R) and potentially the Hired Claw's pump ability ({1}{R}) if the opponent loses life. However, Slickshot costs {1}{R} which uses both Mountains, so they need to play the land first to have mana for Might of the Meek during combat.

At 5 HP, casting Clarion Conqueror (a 3/3 non-haste flyer) instead of Nova Hellkite (4/5 haste flyer that pings a Hired Claw) misses immediate damage and board impact. Playing Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon as the land drop first would provide 5 mana, enough for Nova Hellkite with Momo's discount ({2}{R}{R}), enabling an immediate 4-damage attack plus pinging a Hired Claw.

With the opponent having no untapped blockers, attacking with only 2 creatures instead of all 3 leaves 1-3 free damage on the table. At 5 life vs 18 life, maximizing damage output is important to try to close the gap.

Lethal was available this turn. Cast Nova Hellkite for warp cost {2}{R}, its ETB kills Slickshot Show-Off (the only flying blocker), Momo triggers for +1/+1. Then cast Burst Lightning targeting opponent for 2 damage. Attack with Momo (2/2), two Clarion Conquerors (3/3 each), and Nova Hellkite (4/5 haste) for 12 flying damage + 2 burn = 14 total against opponent's 13 life.

Gem3F Tactic has lethal on board (Momo 1/1 + 2x Clarion Conqueror 3/3 = 7 flying damage vs opponent at 3 HP with no creatures). Casting Charming Prince before combat gives the opponent an unnecessary window to respond with instants before the lethal attack is declared. At 1 HP, gaining 3 life from Prince is reasonable insurance, but standard sequencing says attack for lethal first.
